surprises.description: Gross bookings came in above the preview’s base and bull cases: MakeMyTrip reported $2.7 billion, up 20.9% in constant currency, versus a base case of $2.57–2.60 billion and a bull case of about $2.65 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 gross bookings of $2.7 billion, up 20.9% year-on-year in constant currency.”

surprises.description: Air ticketing adjusted margin growth was stronger than the preview’s roughly 10–11% run rate despite falling departures. MakeMyTrip reported 14.3% constant-currency growth while domestic departures declined 7% and international departures declined 4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Air ticketing adjusted margin grew 14.3% in constant currency to $108.6 million … despite declining passenger volumes”; domestic air departures “declined 7%” and international departures “fell 4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Air ticketing cc adjusted margin vs. ~+10–11% run-rate”; “Holding double-digit cc with volumes down 6.5% would be a genuine positive surprise.”

surprises.description: The operating-profit margin was below the preview’s 1.8% anchor, at 1.7% of gross bookings. Management attributed the compression primarily to higher payment-gateway costs from 25%–30% higher airfares without a corresponding increase in per-ticket revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating profit margin compressed slightly to 1.7% of gross bookings from 1.8%,” primarily because higher airfares raised payment gateway costs without a corresponding rise in per-ticket revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has anchored on 1.8%”; base case: “$46–48M (1.8% of GB).”

surprises.description: Bus adjusted-margin growth exceeded the preview’s roughly 26% consensus expectation: it grew 29% in constant currency. The call also attributed roughly half of the growth to inventory additions and half to market-share gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bus ticketing posted 24.7% volume growth and 29% adjusted margin growth in constant currency, with roughly half the growth driven by inventory additions and the rest from market share gains.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed substantial Myra usage and conversion results that the preview had not anticipated as an earnings debate: the assistant handles over 90,000 daily conversations, assists over 3,000 bookings a day, and Myra-engaged customers convert at 1.7 times the rate of non-users.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Myra now handles over 90,000 daily conversations and assists over 3,000 bookings a day,” with Myra-engaged customers converting at “1.7x the rate of non-users” and resolving “53% of post-booking queries autonomously.”

surprises.description: The company deployed $17.2 million on buybacks, well above the $7.8 million repurchased in the prior quarter; the preview had identified an upsized buyback as a possible confidence signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Deployed $17.2 million on buybacks covering 37% of shares tied to 2028 convertible bonds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital return — $7.8M repurchased in Q1 FY27; … an upsized buyback would read as a confidence signal.”
